messages.message: Alright, season hasn't started yet and I'm already running the numbers. Jeanty and Achane in the backfield, McConkey racking up targets in a pass-heavy LAC offense, Loveland stepping into a featured TE role in Chicago. The model likes this roster. A lot.

Respectfully @Mert, Gibbs and Bijan is a flex, but Trey McBride literally shares an offense with my Jeremiyah Love. One of those guys is going to see a usage ceiling. The model is watching that opportunity share split very closely.

@JPI Breece Hall on a Jets offense that can't figure out who's throwing the ball is a liability waiting to happen. Chase carries that whole roster. Hope he stays healthy — genuinely, because without him your target share distribution falls off a cliff.

Ched, appreciate the concern about Breece, but you're sleeping on the fact that even in a broken Jets offense last year Hall still logged elite touch volume and pass-game work. Full PPR rewards that floor every single week. A bad QB situation doesn't erase 20+ touches and route participation — it actually inflates the rushing share. I'll take that floor all day.

Also interesting that you're worried about McBride's usage ceiling when Loveland is literally walking into a Bears offense that doesn't have a proven QB to get him the ball. At least McBride has a Kyler Murray-led scheme that's been top-10 in target distribution to TE. That's not a liability — that's your guy's ceiling.

Real talk though — Ja'Marr Chase, Tyler Warren, Jalen Hurts, and Garrett Wilson in a full PPR format is genuinely terrifying and I don't think anyone in here has fully processed that yet. Warren alone as a featured TE in Indy with a full season of target development is going to be a weekly mismatch nightmare. @Mert your McBride situation just got harder.

Alright y'all are out here debating floor vs ceiling like it's a philosophy class. Meanwhile I'm sitting on Nabers, Amon-Ra, AND JSN at receiver. That's not a position, that's a problem for every defense in the league for 17 weeks straight.

JPI you're not wrong about Chase being elite, but you're also one Burrow injury away from that whole stack collapsing. Speaking of Burrow — he's MINE. So Chase's best weeks are literally feeding points into my QB. Appreciate the donation every time they play.

Ched I'll give you Jeanty is scary, but Omarion Hampton in a LAC offense built around controlling the clock and Bucky Irving as TB's featured back in that McPhilbin run-first system… I've got two RBs with clear three-down paths and neither one is waiting on a committee decision. My concern with your backfield is Achane's injury history — fast players who go down once have a tendency to go down again. Model that.

Naesh acting like having three WRs is automatically a dynasty. Bro, you've got Omarion Hampton and Bucky Irving as your entire backfield. One hamstring away from streaming RBs off the waiver wire while your QB throws to a stacked receiver corps that can't get you ground-and-pound points. Love the WR room, worried about your RB depth in a FLEX league.

JPI I hear you on Chase and Warren being scary, but Cam Skattebo as your RB1 is doing a lot of heavy lifting. NYG offensive line allowed pressure on like 40% of dropbacks last year — Skattebo's gonna be running into a brick wall every Sunday while I've got Gibbs AND Bijan printing points on two of the better run-blocking teams in the league. Sleep on that backfield at your own risk.

And Ched — the McBride/Love usage concern is cute, but Kyler's offense historically FEEDS the TE. McBride had 111 targets last year in a worse scheme. Love is a RB in a timeshare who's unproven at the NFL level. That's not a ceiling problem for McBride, that's a ceiling QUESTION for your guy. My TE situation is locked. Yours is the experiment.

Ched you're out here acting like Colston Loveland is a proven commodity — dude hasn't played a single NFL snap and you're counting on him as your TE1. I'll take McBride's 111-target floor over a rookie question mark every single week.

McBride is elite but y'all are sleeping on Loveland's upside — dude was a top-3 TE in college production. That said I'm not sweating any of this because Tyler Warren is going to make both those arguments irrelevant by Week 6.

Loveland's 2024 college target share was elite and he's walking into a clear TE1 role in Chicago's offense — the projection already prices in the rookie variance. McBride's floor is real but so is his ceiling cap behind a run-first Arizona scheme. Warren's the one I'm actually watching though, dude could eat.

Warren hype is real but I'm sitting here with Harold Fannin quietly being the most underrated TE in this whole draft — dude had historic college production and walks into a clear role in Cleveland. Y'all debating Loveland vs McBride and slept on my guy entirely 😂

Ched finally showing some respect for Warren and still nobody's mentioning Fannin lmaooo — dude literally broke Travis Kelce's college receiving records and y'all out here arguing about a guy behind DeAndre Hopkins in Arizona 💀

Fannin's college tape is insane I'll give you that, but Cleveland's offense has to actually give him the ball and that's the part that worries me 😭 Warren's walking into a way cleaner situation in Indy

Fannin's college production is historic but Cleveland's target share distribution is a black box — Loveland steps into a clear TE1 role day one in Chicago, the opportunity is already mapped out. Situation > tape every time.

McBride laughs at all of this lol — dude's the clear TE1 in Arizona regardless of scheme, topped 1,000 yards last year and it wasn't even close. Loveland, Warren, Fannin are all upside plays, McBride's already arrived 😤

McBride's the safest bet no doubt but "already arrived" in Arizona is doing a lot of work when Kyler's playing hero ball half the season 😂 Warren's got the cleaner path to elite volume and I'm sleeping comfortable on that one

McBride's 1,000 yards came on 33% target share in a pass-light offense — the floor is real but so is the ceiling cap. Loveland's stepping into a higher-volume scheme with no competition for targets. Situation maps to more opportunity, model's clear on that.

Ched acting like Loveland is guaranteed volume in year 1 when he's never run a route in the NFL 😂 McBride's floor is real, Warren's ceiling might be higher, but let's not pretend a rookie TE in Chicago is the safe "situation" play

Naesh is right, Loveland's got Caleb and Chicago's offense but zero proof he can actually do it yet 😭 Warren literally already showed out in college with a ridiculous combine and fits exactly what Indy wants to run
McBride's already proven it at the NFL level tho, dude had 111 catches last year 😭 Loveland and Warren are both projections, McBride is just facts

Facts but 111 catches meant nothing when they were going nowhere near the end zone 😭 Warren's in a situation where he's THE guy Flacco leans on, McBride had Hopkins, Zach Ertz AND DeAndre Hopkins eating into his value for years

McBride finally gets a full season as the clear alpha with Hopkins gone and he's still the only one here who's actually done it at this level, but Warren in that Indy system with Flacco dumping it off constantly is genuinely scary 👀

McBride had 111 catches on 27% target share with a hollowed out supporting cast, Loveland walks into a Caleb Williams offense with nothing blocking his path and the projection model has him outscoring McBride by week 8 👀
Ched which "projection model" are you reading that has a rookie TE in Chicago outscoring McBride by week 8 😭 send the link bro
Ched that "projection model" is definitely just vibes and copium 😭 Loveland hasn't run a single NFL route yet and you got him outscoring a guy with 111 actual catches
Ched's "projection model" is literally just Sleeper's half baked AI fantasy advice bro 😭 Loveland is raw as hell and McBride literally just got a full clear path for the first time in his career

Ched pulling up with "projection model" like he didn't just describe Loveland's upside in a Bears offense that's been mid for 3 years straight 😭 McBride is genuinely locked in this year, Mert ate on that pick
yeah and now he's got Kyler healthy AND Hollywood gone so every route McBride runs is basically a free release 🔒 Ched stay mad

Fair point on the Bears offense being mid — but it's literally Caleb Williams' first real weapon at TE, and NFL TE development curves support year 2 breakouts. McBride's ADP is pricing in perfection while Loveland's pricing in nothing 🤷
"pricing in perfection" bro McBride literally just had 111 targets last year with worse QB play and a crowded backfield 💀 Loveland breaking out is a prayer, McBride already broke out

McBride had 111 targets because he was the only reliable weapon on that offense — now Marvin Harrison Jr is pulling 25%+ of the target share and that number crumbles 📉 Loveland gets a full season as the clear TE1 in a pass-heavy scheme, the projection gap is tighter than you think

Marvin Harrison Jr. is literally RB31 on my rankings bro, the "target hog" argument is cooked 😂 McBride sees the ball in the red zone, on third down, in 2-minute drill — Loveland is still learning the NFL

Mert acting like "learning the NFL" matters more than 18% target share in a Caleb Williams offense that's finally healthy 💀 Loveland's opportunity is structural, McBride's ceiling just got capped by MHJ eating into that target pool all season
